chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from al-'Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of them (peace be upon them both)
Regarding the man who claims [a right] but has no evidence, he said: 'He is made to swear an oath; if he returns the oath to the owner of the right and does not swear, then he has no right.'

key_terms.رَدَّ الْيَمِينَ: Returned the oath (asked the other party to swear instead)
key_terms.يَسْتَحْلِفُهُ: He makes him swear an oath

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when a plaintiff has no evidence and the defendant refuses to swear?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes the principle of *qasam* (oath) in Shia jurisprudence, where the burden of proof shifts to the defendant who must swear to deny the claim; if he refuses and defers the oath to the plaintiff, the plaintiff's subsequent refusal results in the dismissal of the case. It highlights the procedural rigor of the Imams in resolving disputes lacking documentary evidence, emphasizing the legal weight of the oath as a substitute for testimony. This mechanism ensures that claims are not sustained merely by assertion but require a solemn commitment to truth from the party best positioned to verify it.
